item.title: Tens of thousands protest across Portugal over soaring housing costs
item.description: Protests occurred in over 30 cities across Portugal, reflecting increasing frustration over rising housing costs and insufficient incomes. Many protesters, including students and professionals, expressed concern about the affordability of housing. Demonstrators called for stronger tenant protections and limits on rent increases amidst growing inequality. The government promised to implement measures for affordable housing but acknowledged that changes will take time.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: UK PM Burnham's speechwriter caught using ChatGPT to draft speech
item.description: An anonymous speechwriter for Prime Minister Andy Burnham was seen using ChatGPT to draft a keynote address. The speech focused on criticizing former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's legacy and addressing the cost-of-living crisis. Burnham emphasized the importance of these issues during his talk with Welsh Labour members. Opposition members have criticized both the aide's actions and Burnham’s government's plans to address economic challenges.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: US judge halts Trump's plan to close historic DC golf course for redevelopment
item.description: A US judge has issued a temporary block on President Trump's plan to close East Potomac Park. The ruling comes amid a legal challenge regarding the redevelopment of the historic public golf course. US District Judge Ana Reyes found that the government violated federal laws in seeking the closure. Trump plans to replace the existing courses with an 18-hole championship-level facility for major tournaments.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women
item.description: Men gathered in the Swiss capital to protest against misogyny and violence directed at women. The demonstration called for men to take an active role in opposing misogynistic views, especially online. Organizers stressed the need for men to acknowledge their responsibility in challenging these attitudes. The event followed increased awareness of violence committed by men, highlighting the importance of addressing harmful masculinity.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Hamas confirms death of senior commander Samir Abu Younis in Israeli airstrike
item.description: In a recent Israeli airstrike, senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, an incident that also left many injured. Known for his involvement in the planning of the deadly October 7 assault on Israel, his funeral is set for Sunday. The ongoing conflict continues to claim significant casualties on both sides since the ceasefire in October 2025.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Prince William, Kate to arrive in India in first joint overseas tour since 2022
item.description: Kate Middleton will join Prince William in Mumbai for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards event. This visit marks their first overseas engagement together since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The awards will bring together notable personalities and focus on environmental challenges and innovation. Kate has been gradually returning to public life after her recovery, which has had its challenges.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Jimothy Card Auction: Rare card sells for $20,100; proceeds may fund Abby’s college
item.description: A young baseball enthusiast from Seattle secured an esteemed baseball card during a Mariners game. This unique card showcased Jimothy, a raccoon who captured the internet's attention due to his extraordinary look. Initially a complimentary giveaway, the card has now emerged as a remarkable collectible valued at an astonishing $20,100. With multiple offers pouring in, her family decided to auction it on eBay, generating significant buzz.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A bronze leg found in 1820 considered Roman loot now believed to belong to a statue of Antoninus Pius
item.description: Emperor Antoninus Pius, celebrated for his peace-driven rule and military expeditions, may have a newly discovered connection to history. A bronze leg unearthed in Scotland suggests a statue that honored him was disassembled by Roman forces prior to their withdrawal in AD 161, challenging prior beliefs of theft. This discovery sheds light on how Rome strategically managed its monuments, and further archaeological investigations could reveal more insights.

item.title: Pennsylvania father barred mother from daughters' school photos and tennis matches; court upheld her authority
item.description: In a recent custody case between John M Surma and Julie S Surma, a Pennsylvania court affirmed that the mother retains primary authority over extracurricular activities. The evidence presented indicated that the father imposed limitations on her involvement in various school events. John Surma expressed concerns that this ruling diminished his influence on his daughters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 10-year-old boy noticed his father's speech slurring during a drive; helps his dad survive a stroke
item.description: During a road trip to Georgia, Taylor Fritts showcased incredible presence of mind when his father suffered a stroke. While driving in Sweetwater, Tennessee, he observed his father's peculiar speech and actions. Without hesitation, Taylor contacted emergency services, leading to a swift hospital transfer via helicopter. His bravery earned him recognition as a 'Stroke Champion', highlighting the unbreakable bond between father and son.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2024, New Jersey began restoring a 290-acre marsh and former industrial site
item.description: Cape May County has launched an ambitious restoration project aimed at revitalizing its local ecosystem. By focusing on rejuvenating tidal flow and creating new wildlife habitats, the area is already witnessing the return of various aquatic prey and bird species. The initiative also includes protective measures for freshwater ecosystems, promoting a balanced environment while enhancing public access with newly built trails and recreational facilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Texas appeals court upholds sale of marital home despite wife's challenge to $685,000 offer
item.description: In a Texas court, a woman expressed her discontent with the ruling permitting a receiver to sell her marital home. The appellate court upheld the initial decision, dismissing her objections to the receiver's role in accepting a $685,000 offer for the house. The ruling clarified that her financial stake did not afford her control over the sale, highlighting the need for precise wording in divorce agreements related to property transactions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 2 Infants buried in Peru about 1,600 years ago; one had a rare fatal birth defect called cyclopia
item.description: In southern Peru, archaeologists uncovered the remains of two infants buried together, one exhibiting cyclopia. Genetic analysis confirmed that the infant with cyclopia had trisomy 13, a chromosomal condition. Their burial in a single ceramic vessel reveals insights into ancient funerary practices. Researchers highlighted that the infant's condition did not result in unusual treatment in life or death. This discovery emphasizes the historical presence of congenital differences in human populations.

item.title: Florida court upholds removal of daughter who represented estate and trusts without a lawyer
item.description: In a recent ruling, Kerrin Friedman faced a significant legal setback when the Florida Third District Court of Appeal upheld her removal as personal representative of her mother’s estate and trustee of three family trusts. Her failure to comply with court mandates for legal counsel led to this decision, emphasizing her inability to manage the estate and trust affairs without proper authorization.
